lead_headline: Restaurant churn slows to 1 new lead Saturday—Lakewood SNARF's opening confirmed—as active roster ticks to 54 (26 openings, 28 closures)

restaurant.blurb: 1 new lead today bumps active roster to 54 total (26 openings, 28 closures)—opening side adds SNARF's Sandwiches expansion to Belmar/Lakewood (Barnum West, Colorado chain's 'coming soon' location per official website). Week's notable debuts: Vaultaire's subterranean HiFi lounge (Speer, beneath La Forêt, opened Thursday), FiNO Mediterranean tapas (City Park, All Inn Hotel's restaurant component, soft opened Tuesday), Mendocino Farms' Highland location (West Highland, launched Monday), Bad Rabbit Coffee's brick-and-mortar (Cole, early March). Closure side tallies Super Mega Bien's permanent close (Five Points, 8-year RiNo fixture shuttered March 14 citing financial pressure). Geographic churn: Union Station sees continued vendor rotation, City Park gains dining density via hotel conversions, West Highland captures chain expansion attention. Openings pull 2-lead deficit to closures—26 vs 28, tightest gap since mid-February.

foreclosure.blurb: 42 new filings this week climb 40% from prior week's 30—sharpest week-over-week acceleration since late January breaks two-week March softness. 106 auctions scheduled next seven days hold near-term pipeline stable, but $71M total exposure compresses 14% as mega-filing volume dries up post-Arapahoe's $57M South Vaughn outlier. Only one seven-figure case this week: $794K County Road 96 (Weld, scheduled). County distribution: El Paso leads at 475 active, Weld climbs to 431, Arapahoe slides to 451. Filing count's 42% weekly jump signals March volatility persists—30-72 filing band replaces January's 50+ steady-state as baseline fractures into boom-bust pattern.

reputation.blurb: 1 mention today drags seven-day total to 40 citations across 11 sources—down 11% from prior week's 45, marking second consecutive weekly decline. Denver Post maintains iron grip with 18 of 40 pickups (45% share, up from 43% prior week), social platforms deliver 13 mentions (Instagram 6, Facebook 7), Hoodline trails at 3. Saturday's lone detection: McNichols Civic Center Building Instagram post. Week's source concentration deepens: Post plus social aggregates command 78% of total volume—single-outlet dependency intensifies as niche publishers fade. Discovery remains 100% Google News RSS. Monthly pace: 122 total through 21 days projects 169-mention March if sustained, tracking 39% above February.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +3 yesterday (4 new, 1 canceled) pushes MTD to +34 (+1.7/day), 90-day cumulative at +98. Friday's 4-1 split extends clean retention streak—past five days average 0.8 cancellations/day vs March's 1.4/day overall. Seven-day window: +17 net (23 new, 6 canceled) matches prior week's +17 exactly, third consecutive week holding 15-17 net band—acquisition steadies at 3-4 daily baseline post-March 9's 8-new outlier. March's 1.7/day rate tracks 31% above YTD's 1.3/day benchmark, strongest monthly performance on record. Recent pattern: two-week stabilization after early-month volatility, cancellations compress toward 1/day floor while new subscriber flow normalizes at 3-5 daily range.
